name: The Detent Congregation

detectability.signature: Chitinous click-chorus in lockstep rhythm with EM spikes resembling a single vast attention

proximity: Scout organisms detach from the ring to orbit intruders at a fixed remove
Sensors register electromagnetic patterns resembling one vast, patient attention
contact: Boarding filaments tap hulls in probing rhythms, testing every seam and seal
Pheromone-like signatures mark vessels for later retrieval
prolonged_exposure: Parasitic infestation as larvae ride the boarding filaments inside
Crew behavioral changes progress into collective obedience toward the ring

phenomena: Bioluminescent displays flashing in lockstep across thousands of bodies
Electromagnetic patterns resembling neural activity centered on the ring
Pheromone-like chemical signatures trailing behind the swarm
opportunities: Contact with alien intelligence should communication be achieved
Recovery of lost ships incorporated intact into the ring's lattice
known_incidents: The dredger Clasp and Paw joined the ring in 2296; her crew walked out eight days later, in step and smiling
description: Twelve million organisms hold formation as a ring ninety million kilometers across, each carapace edged in blue bioluminescence that flashes in perfect lockstep. From a distance the Congregation looks like a jeweled gasket around a dead moon; from closer, it looks back. Sensors within a million kilometers pick up EM patterns neurologists describe as a single attention wearing a swarm.

The ring rotates on a nineteen-day cycle, but its responses obey no schedule scouts have found: sometimes visitors are orbited politely for weeks, and sometimes boarding filaments deploy within minutes, tapping hulls like fingers testing a lock. Marked vessels find themselves revisited seasons later. The swarm's interest never seems to expire, only to wait.

Colonial biologists classify it as a natural superorganism that has been incorporating derelicts into its lattice for millions of years, which makes the intact ships visible in the ring either architecture or larder. The dredger Clasp and Paw joined the structure in 2296; her crew walked out eight days later in step, smiling, and unable to explain the word 'detent.'

A permanent quarantine buoy chain circles the swarm at two radii, and every expedition since 2296 has ended with either new specimens or new vacancies. Linguists persist, convinced the lockstep flashes encode grammar rather than appetite. Recovery teams, meanwhile, keep pricing out salvage contracts on the forty-one ships visibly embedded in the lattice.
